terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. The demo runs each task in turn, with a declined card and a silent tracker among them.

tasks.title: Catch a declined card
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/payments.js`, make `tryPayment(order)` charge `order.totalCents` with `chargeCard` and give back a promise of one line: `'WC-4001 paid, code A-301'` when the charge goes through, and `'WC-4002 not paid: Card declined'`, with the message of the error, when it fails. Its promise is never rejected. The lesson shows how with `try` and `catch` around `await`.

Check hands `tryPayment` a card machine of its own that goes through or fails when Check says so.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's parts on a failed promise and on `try` and `catch` around `await`.
Make `tryPayment` an `async` function with a `try` and a `catch`.
Inside the `try`, wait for the charge and return the paid line.
Inside the `catch`, return the not paid line, and run the demo.
hints: A declined card makes the promise from `chargeCard` fail, and `await` throws that failure on the line where it waits.
The `catch` only sees the failure when the `await` is inside the `try`. The words of the failure are in `error.message`.
The shape is `try { const receipt = await chargeCard(order.totalCents); return ... } catch (error) { return ... }`, inside an `async` function.

videos.title: What happens when a promise fails

tasks.title: Catch at the end of a chain
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, make `parcelOrUnknown(parcelId)` give back a promise of the parcel's id and status from `trackParcel`, like `'P-77: out for delivery'`. When the tracker fails, the promise is fulfilled with `'P-99: no news yet'` instead, with the id it was given. Write it as a chain with `then` and `catch`, without `async` or `await`.

Check hands `parcelOrUnknown` a tracker of its own that answers or fails when Check says so, and reads your function for the `catch`.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on `catch` at the end of a chain.
Start from `trackParcel(parcelId)` and make the line in a `then`.
Add a `catch` after the `then`, with a function that gives back the no news line.
Give back the whole chain, and run the demo.
hints: The tracker's failure skips every `then` and lands in the first `catch` after them.
What the function you hand `catch` gives back is what the promise is fulfilled with. A `catch` placed before the `then` hands its line on to that `then`.

tasks.title: Try again
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, make `chargeWithRetries(totalCents, tries)` charge `totalCents` with `chargeCard`, and when a charge fails, try again, one try after the other, until a charge goes through or it has tried `tries` times. Its promise is fulfilled with the first receipt that goes through. When every try fails, it is rejected with the error of the last try.

Check hands it a card machine of its own that fails as many times as Check says, and counts the charges and when each one started.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on trying again.
Write a loop that runs at most `tries` times.
Inside it, `try` to return the awaited charge, and in the `catch` keep the error.
After the loop, pass the last error on with `throw`.
hints: Each try has to wait for the one before, so the charge is awaited inside the loop. A `return` ends the function as soon as one goes through.
A failed try must not end the function: catch it, keep its error in a `let` made before the loop, and let the loop go round again. Without a `throw` at the end, the caller would think it worked.
The shape is `for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= tries; attempt++) { try { return await chargeCard(totalCents) } catch (error) { lastError = error } }`, then `throw lastError`.

tasks.title: Turn the screen off either way
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, make `payWithScreen(order)` call `screenOn`, charge `order.totalCents` with `chargeCard`, and call `screenOff` once the machine has answered, whether the charge went through or failed. Its promise is fulfilled with the receipt, or rejected with the machine's error: the failure still reaches whoever called `payWithScreen`.

Check hands it a card machine and a screen of its own, and looks at when the screen was turned on and off, and what the promise did.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on cleaning up either way.
Wait for the charge inside a `try`, and turn the screen off in a `finally`.
Run the demo: the screen goes off after both the paid and the declined order.
hints: Turning the screen off belongs to both endings, the receipt and the failure. Writing it after the `await` only covers the first.
`finally` runs after the `try` either way, and without a `catch` the failure carries on to the caller once it has run.
The shape is `screenOn()`, then `try { return await chargeCard(order.totalCents) } finally { screenOff() }`, inside an `async` function.
